title: act-mcp .evidence run manifest (.evidence/runs/<run_id>/meta.json), schema_version 1
description: One manifest per act-mcp run, written LAST (after act finished and after the evidence records were published), so a present meta.json means the run reached a terminal state. This file is audit/debug context, NOT the load-bearing contract: downstream cross-commit scanners read only .evidence/{benchmark,coverage}/**.jsonl. A run directory without meta.json means the process died mid-run (treat every file in that directory as suspect). See docs/adr/0002-evidence-jsonl-contract.md section 1.3.

schema_version.description: Manifest contract version, bumped under the same rules as the record schema.

status.description: Terminal run state. Same vocabulary as the record envelope's run_status, plus 'running' is never valid here (the manifest is written only at termination).

commit.description: Full commit SHA the run was attributed to. Matches the <full-sha> directory the evidence records were filed under.

exit_code.description: act process exit status; absent when act produced no exit status.

act.description: How act was invoked. argv is stored with secret values already redacted to the literal '***' (never a secret); 'log' points at the verbatim act --json stream for this run.

incoming.description: The per-run payload directory the job wrote through the bind mount. 'files' lists what survived: files that parsed successfully are deleted at the end of the run, so non-empty 'files' means unparsed or suspect payload kept for debugging (ADR-0002 section 3).

removed.description: True when the payload directory was cleaned up after extraction.

payload.description: The payload this run actually read, kept under runs/<run_id>/payload/ so the file a coverage or benchmark record was computed from outlives the scratch directory it arrived in. The records' own source_path names the scratch path the extractor read from; this member names where that file now lives. Absent when nothing was read, or when retention is off (--max-payload-keep-bytes 0). 'dropped' counts consumed payload the per-run byte budget would not fit, deleted instead of kept. See docs/adr/0002-evidence-jsonl-contract.md section 3.4.

bytes.description: Total size of the files kept, which never exceeds 'cap_bytes'.

cap_bytes.description: The --max-payload-keep-bytes budget in force for this run.

path.description: File name inside 'dir', not a path: the payload directory is flat.

dropped.description: Consumed payload deleted rather than kept, because the budget would not fit it or it could not be moved. Non-zero pairs with the payload_cap_exceeded warning.

evidence.description: What this run published. Empty array is legitimate (category with no evidence, or extraction found nothing) and is how 'ran but produced nothing' is distinguishable from 'never ran'.

malformed.description: Count of well-formed-but-unusable inputs seen while extracting (bad marker lines, unparseable metric rows). Never a run failure.

warnings.description: Machine-readable warning codes for this run (no_coverage_found, parse_failed, payload_too_large, payload_unreadable, malformed_metric, truncated, payload_cap_exceeded, ...). Open vocabulary.

relpath.description: Workspace-relative path with '/' separators, no leading '/', no '.' or '..' segments.
